content: Nutrition for men encompasses the study of dietary requirements, physiological impacts, and practical health implications tailored to male biology and health risks. It focuses on specific nutrient needs influenced by male hormonal profiles, body composition, and susceptibility to certain chronic diseases such as cardiovascular disease, prostate cancer, and metabolic syndrome. Mechanistically, nutrition affects male physiology by modulating hormone synthesis, energy metabolism, muscle protein synthesis, bone integrity, and neurological function. Key nutrient categories include macronutrients—proteins, carbohydrates, and fats—and micronutrients such as zinc, magnesium, vitamin D, and B vitamins, all critical for maintaining male reproductive and systemic health. Practical relevance arises in designing diet plans that support testosterone levels, optimize body composition, prevent obesity, and mitigate risks of common male health issues. Nutrition for men is also synonymous with male-specific diet optimization, men's dietary health, and male-targeted nutritional strategies. Limitations in this field include variable individual nutrition responses due to genetics, lifestyle factors, and underlying health conditions. Safety considerations involve avoiding excessive supplementation that can disrupt hormonal balance or cause toxicity. Evidence supporting men's nutrition recommendations is evolving, drawn from epidemiological, clinical trials, and physiological studies but requires further male-specific randomized controlled trials for confirmation.
